utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. The case number, IT-98-32-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner representing the Prosecution together with Ann Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. For the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Vladimir Domazet, counsel of Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vasiljevic, are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down. This is a Status Conference held in accordance with the provisions of Rule 65 and within the time limit imposed by that Rule. Ms. Korner, what is happening about the disclosure of the supporting material?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the supporting material was disclosed to Mr. Domazet some time ago when he came onto the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. I remember you were waiting until counsel was appointed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you remember what date it was?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Off the top of my head I can't, no. I'm sure Ms. Sutherland will be able to assist me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Was it in a language the accused understands?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Can I mention on that topic, Your Honour, this: The disclosure took place with the name and any information which might identify the witnesses redacted. However, that is how it went before the Confirming Judge. So in this case, as opposed to another case which Your Honour is seized of, the supporting material is in identical form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Good. Thank you very much. I rather suspected that might be the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, could I say this: We served upon the Court, if that's the right word, lodged with the Court a motion for protective measures in identical terms to the one which has been put in place in the case of Brdjanin and Talic. That was given to counsel who originally represented Mr. Vasiljevic, but I understand from speaking to Mr. Domazet very briefly this morning that he never received it, and Your Honour will have seen there's been no response lodged to that motion within the time period, but I think that's because Mr. Domazet's never had it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. What about the -- any additional statements from -- what is it? -- Rule 66(A)(ii)?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I put Your Honour in the picture straight away? Some further statements have been taken. They're in the process of being translated. They will be disclosed to the Defence as soon as that is done, and effective, Your Honour, this case is ready to go any time that this Trial Chamber orders it, so far as the Prosecution is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: When do you expect to serve these further statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It will be a question of the translation department. As Your Honour may know, it's very overburdened in the moment. We would hope within the next two to three weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. Thank you very much. Well, Mr. Domazet, when were you served with the supporting material, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Your Honour, it was about 15 February, I think, 15 or 16. I was here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Does that mean, from your silence, that we are not going to have an application under Rule 72 in relation to the form of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. That means we're not going to get any application. Thank you very much. Now, is there any matter which you wish to raise within the terms of Rule 65 in relation to your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I'm awaiting additional materials and we are preparing our witnesses and the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But you are familiar, are you, with the terms of Rule 65 bis as to the matters which you are entitled to raise on behalf of your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And there's nothing further you want to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, is there anything that either party wishes to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Only this, Your Honour, and it doesn't really particularly apply, but the question of protective measures does apply to a number of cases, and I think it would assist if we were to have some idea of when we were likely to get a ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Hopefully soon. The draft is well under way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If I may remind you -- probably you do not need reminding, Ms. Korner, but there is the continuing obligation which the Prosecution has under Rule 66, 67, and 68, and no doubt you'll keep it in mind should anything further arise. Nothing further you wish to raise, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. About this 65 bis, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That so --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. May I just mention one other matter. I think it may assist the Court to know that not only do we anticipate being in a position to go; Pre-Trial brief will be begun and lodged quite soon. But it's a very short case. We anticipate that the Prosecution case will take no more than about 14 days in all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So that if we have a slot for a short case, this is a good candidate.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Absolutely. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. I'm not holding out any promises, I should say, but it's a very good idea to have a case ready to run at short notice, hopefully.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Sutherland reminds me, correctly, that perhaps if the Registry were to provide Mr. Domazet with a copy of the motion, because he hasn't had it, would Your Honour say that he could then have 14 days from today to respond if he so wishes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That depends on whether he will be served with it today.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I merely raised it to assist Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I understand that. Well, just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll seek to ensure that Mr. Domazet gets a copy of that motion today, and we'll extend the time for 14 days from today in which to respond to that motion for protective measures. That's all. Thank you very much for attending, and we'll adjourn.
